features.summary: Firefox improved how WebRTC (the technology behind video calls) selects video encoders on Android. The system now prioritizes the phone's built-in hardware encoders—specialized circuits that compress video efficiently—over software compression, which saves battery and improves call quality. The changes also ensure codec plugins are available before attempting to create them, preventing failures.

features.summary: Several internal improvements to WebRTC peer connection handling: better memory management for RTCDataChannel objects to prevent them from being accidentally freed while calls are active, **clearer error reporting when SCTP (the protocol behind data channels) connections fail**, and support for setting maximum data channels and configuring data transport in different call states. The changes also refactored codec and RTP (the protocol that carries audio and video) header storage for consistency.

features.summary: Firefox now supports **AV1 hardware encoding in WebRTC when your device has it**, providing better compression for video calls. The system prioritizes the phone's hardware encoders for efficiency, improved codec plugin availability checks, and rerouted MediaCapabilities checks through a more reliable async codec support path for consistent codec discovery.

features.summary: Improved how Firefox establishes WebRTC connections (ICE, the mechanism that finds the best path between peers, and DTLS, which encrypts the connection). patches.subject: Bug 2063717, part 2 - Replace uses of services::GetAsyncShutdownService().

patches.subject: Part 1: Unify IPDL actor devirutalization logic, and require types to be fully qualified,

patches.subject: Cleanup default state for static-analysis on Windows / dom part

features.label: Common

patches.author: Michael Froman
patches.subject: Expose the webrtc port allowlist as a shared IsWebrtcPortAllowed helper.

patches.author: Nicolas Grunbaum
patches.subject: fully support extmap-allow-mixed;r=bwc

features.summary: Two improvements to WebRTC connection reliability: a shared security policy ensuring WebRTC only uses authorized ports, and full support for extmap-allow-mixed, an advanced SDP (session description) option that enables more flexible RTP header extensions during negotiations.

features.label: Negotiation engine (JSEP)

patches.author: Philipp Hancke
patches.subject: implement RTCConfiguration.alwaysNegotiateDataChannels

patches.author: Nicolas Grunbaum
patches.subject: Add distinct errors for SDP parsing failures.

features.summary: Firefox added better error reporting for WebRTC connection negotiation by providing distinct error types for SDP parsing failures, making debugging easier. It also supports the RTCConfiguration.alwaysNegotiateDataChannels option for more predictable connection setup.

features.label: Session negotiation (SDP)

patches.author: Nicolas Grunbaum
patches.subject: update rsdparsa_capi to use webrtc-sdp 0.3.14;r=mjf

patches.author: Sylvestre Ledru
patches.subject: Restore ostream format state in SDP imageattr serialization (Coverity CID 1315812, 1315813, 1315814)

features.summary: Internal updates to SDP (the format WebRTC uses to negotiate video calls): support for a newer version of the SDP parsing library and a fix for output formatting in image attribute serialization.

features.label: WebRTC tests

patches.author: Michael Froman
patches.subject: add checkRemoteCandidatePorts to test_peerConnection_portRestrictions.html

patches.author: Byron Campen
patches.subject: Perform state-checking before comparison against last created description.

features.summary: WebRTC tests were updated to be more reliable and to verify port-restriction behavior: tests now check internal connection state before comparing descriptions and include a test that verifies remote ICE candidate ports are constrained by the browser's allowlist. This helps ensure the port-restriction enforcement works as intended and reduces flakiness in automated testing.

features.label: Objc Video Capture

patches.author: Michael Froman
patches.subject: Bug 2058693 (MOZ) - upstream removed a header

features.summary: Objective‑C video capture code was updated to follow an upstream change that removed a header. This keeps the macOS/iOS camera-capture code compiling and compatible with newer platform headers; _no visible user change_, just necessary maintenance to avoid build breakage.

features.label: Video Engine

patches.author: Timothy Nikkel
patches.subject: Bug 2058388. Allow passing the DrawView flag to drawSnapshot so root scrollbars are painted, and so reftest's snapshot path matches its default one.

features.summary: _No visible change_—an internal improvement to Firefox's video rendering snapshot feature to better handle scrollbars during automated testing.
